global_recent.title: The Belém Call: Mobilizing Finance for Forest Protection
global_recent.description: Join us today for a webinar exploring the Belém Call to Action for the Congo Basin Forests, a landmark initiative launched at COP30 that mobilizes over USD 2.5 billion to halt and reverse deforestation by 2030. The Congo Basin—home to the world’s second-largest tropical rainforest—plays a vital role in global climate regulation, biodiversity, and local livelihoods. This session will unpack the Call’s objectives, financing, and alignment with the Congo Basin Forest Partnership roadmap, and discuss what it means in practice for governments, Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and partners working to turn this commitment into lasting impact.

global_recent.title: Indigenous NDCs for Climate Justice in the Amazon Basin
global_recent.description:
Made with Restream. Livestream on 30+ platforms at once via https://restream.io

As COP30 in Belém, Brazil quickly approaches, Indigenous Peoples are continuing to rise to the forefront of global climate leadership. The first of its kind and rooted in ancestral knowledge, the Indigenous NDC reinforces that the climate debate must consider equity, self-determination, and the effective participation of Indigenous Peoples in the implementation of Brazil’s and Colombia’s NDCs under the Paris Agreement. This webinar will examine how these climate commitments can center the territorial rights of Indigenous Peoples.

global_recent.title: Why are common reporting standards important for tracking funds directed to IPLCs?
Why are organisational financial capacities crucial for tenure rights?
global_recent.description:
The climate and biodiversity crises have forced the world to pledge billions of dollars to mitigate the impact of environmental degradation, a significant portion of which should be heading for Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descedant and local communities as they have sustained their own communities and forests for generations.  

As long-term partners with Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant and local community organisations’ Tenure Facility has listened deeply to their needs. Overtime, they have shown us their keen interest to learn ‘conventional’ ways of handling finances to better protect their space, as securing their land and forest rights requires substantial financial resources and stable financial systems.

In 2024, Tenure Facility, with the support of Spring Strategies, kickstarted the Financial Training Programme to provide partners in Latin America with effective finance and administrative tools, strengthened financial capacities to enable them to acquire more funds, and guidance in the implementation of their plans.

global_recent.title: What is the meaning that the Amazon forest holds for you? Amazon Community Funds Learning Exchange
global_recent.description: Sandra Ribeiro (left) and Helena Gomes (right) were participants and community representatives at the July Learning Exchange on Amazon Community Funds which took place in Esperantina, Piaui, Brazil at the beginning of July 2024. Sandra and Helena are from the Cooperative of the Interstate Movement of the Babaçu Coconut Breakers (MIQCB). They share their words and reflect on the important role the Amazon forest plays for them.

global_recent.title: Why investing in Indigenous women?
global_recent.description:
Did you know that traditional knowledge, often preserved by Indigenous women, is vital for climate resilience?

We hear from @sara.omic, an Emberá Lawyer and Indigenous Rights advocate from Panama, who explains how her community turned to medicinal plants during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the importance of protecting our forests and the wisdom they hold.

Supporting Indigenous women means investing in a sustainable future and preserving cultural heritage. Learn more about the impact of ancestral knowledge on climate action and community well-being. 

🌿 This 3-part video series is a collaboration between @globalalliancet and @TenureFacility.
What kind of world will you help build?
#IndigenousWomen #PreservingPlanet #GuardiansOfTomorrow 📸 @ifnotusthenwho

global_recent.title: Gender and biodiversity: How Indigenous and Local Community Women Safeguard Nature - Land Dialogue
global_recent.description:
Indigenous women's knowledge is rooted in a deep appreciation of the natural world. They possess an intricate understanding of various species, their nutritional value, medicinal properties, and ecological roles. This knowledge passed down through generations, not only enriches their communities but has been crucial for science.

Despite this, Indigenous women often remain marginalised and relegated to the status of beneficiaries rather than recognised as partners and agents of change.

As we look forward to COP16 and discussions surrounding the Global Biodiversity Framework, amplifying their voices and integrating their perspectives into global dialogues on benefit-sharing and biodiversity conservation becomes increasingly important.

Hear from Indigenous leaders on how to best support and recognise women as the custodians of traditional knowledge systems.

global_recent.title: How Indigenous and local community women safeguard nature
global_recent.description:
Turn your videos into live streams with Restream https://restre.am/ANIm

Join us on June 13, 2024, from 9:00 AM to 10:15 AM EST for a webinar that delves into the profound knowledge Indigenous women possess about the natural world. This event will explore how their ancestral understanding and holistic approach have contributed to both their communities and Western science, informing the development of medicines and enhancing our understanding of climate phenomena. Despite their crucial role, Indigenous women often face marginalization. As we approach COP16, this webinar aims to highlight the importance of integrating their perspectives into global biodiversity conservation efforts for more effective and inclusive outcomes.

global_recent.title: Women Ancestral Knowledge - GATC & TF campaign
global_recent.description:
We’re celebrating the powerful role of Indigenous women in preserving ancestral knowledge and protecting our environment.

Featuring interview snippets from Balkisou Buba, vice national coordinator of REPALEAC, she shares profound insights on how Indigenous women practice sustainable conservation and highlights the unique skills Indigenous women possess as skilled geographers and climate forecasters.

🍃 Discover how traditions, passed through generations, are essential for maintaining a sustainable future. This 3-part video series is a collaboration with @globalalliancet and @thetenurefacility.
What kind of world will you help build?
#IndigenousWomen #PreservingPlanet #GuardiansOfTomorrow 📸 @ifnotusthenwho

BRA.title: Inter-State Movement of Babassu Coconut Breakers in  Piauí
BRA.description:
Vila Esperança, State of Piauí, Brazil, our partner, the Inter-State Movement of Babassu Coconut Breakers, promotes the implementation of 3 state and 18 municipal “free babassu” laws, which protect babassu palms and give women the right to harvest them anywhere.

🇧🇷Securing the boundaries and safeguarding the ancestral lands of Indigenous Peoples, Quilombolas, and local communities, while upholding the laws, ensuring free access to babassu palms for communities, or protecting forests from destruction, is not merely a matter of respecting tenure rights - it is the cornerstone of effective conservation in the Brazilian Amazon. 

🌎 Strong tenure rights protect traditional forest guardianship, which is pivotal in combatting climate change. By entrusting forests to community management, we fortify their role as powerful stewards making a significant positive impact on the planet's climate.

BRA.title: Rapid deforestation of the Amazon could influence temperatures over the Tibetan plateau
BRA.description:
📃From New Scientist : Saini Yang at Beijing Normal University in China and her colleagues analysed global climatological data from 1979 to 2019 to identify correlations in temperature and precipitation between the Amazon rainforest and other areas. Such links are called “teleconnections”.

❗️They focused on the Amazon rainforest in particular because of its significance as a major carbon sink and as a climatic “tipping point” that could see forest turn to savannah beyond a certain threshold of warming and human-driven deforestation. 

🔥The researchers found that since 1979, warm temperatures in the Amazon correlated with warm temperatures over the Tibetan plateau and the West Antarctic ice sheet; more precipitation in the Amazon was associated with less precipitation in those regions.

📉By analysing changing temperatures in the regions between the Amazon and those distant areas, they were also able to trace the path through which energy or materials such as black carbon released in forest fires might propagate through the atmosphere.

BRA.title: Eli Virkina: International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples
BRA.description:
Celebrating the future on 2023's International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples.

Eli Virkina is a member of the Santu Urku Kichwa community on the Napo River in the Ecuadorian Amazon. As a Kichwa artist, environmental scientist, and storyteller, she is inspired by the land and people who shaped her but worries about its protection for the next generation.

COD.title: Stories of resilience- Democratic Republic of Congo
COD.description:
DRC:
Early in 2020 our partners were busy preparing for the June launch of the Tenure Facility-backed project, which will see communities being supported to make use of a new ministerial order on communal lands to secure 300,000 hectares of forestlands in western DRC. With the arrival of the pandemic however, already isolated villages found themselves more cut off than ever through lock down. Already impoverished communities have gone hungry, and whilst there has been little spread of the virus itself, fear of its impacts has proved to be an infection of its own. Despite this, our partners have shown resilience and adaptability to these changing circumstances while moving forward.

Day 1 - DRC - Garantir les droits d'occupation: Assurer des titres fonciers pour les CL/PA
Rolling back social and environmental safeguards in the name of COVID-19 Recorded Webinar
COD.description:
Global leaders increasingly recognise that land rights for indigenous and local communities are a prerequisite for achieving national and international goals for forest governance, food security, climate mitigation, economic development and human rights.

In 2020, however, the COVID-19 pandemic shifted the political context in many countries, and some governments used the pandemic as a justification for dismantling the protections gained by Indigenous and Forest Peoples. This has been particularly common in heavily forested countries where there are large indigenous communities. In this webinar, experts talked about how the roll back has affected safeguards, particularly in these five country-specific reports on Brazil, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Indonesia, and Perú. These reports address the following question: Since the outbreak of COVID-19, to what extent are the five most tropically forested countries rolling back social and environmental safeguards and if so, what are, or may be, the negative consequences in terms of land grabs, rights abuse and deforestation in indigenous territories.

COL.title: "Territory Is Life" - Collective Land Titling in Colombia
Day 1 - Colombia - Observatorio de Derechos territoriales de los Pueblos Indigenas
Stories of resilience- Colombia PCN
COL.description: First arriving in South America as slaves during a brutal colonial period, Afro-descendant communities in Colombia have over the centuries developed deep ties to the land they have worked and lived upon. Afro-descendant organisations are well used to operating in the volatile and complex world of Colombian politics. Nonetheless, Coronavirus has created new challenges. Realising that the situation was likely to remain serious for some time, the Tenure Facility’s partners looked to change the way they worked, and the way they interacted with communities, creating new ways of bringing forward their land rights’ project.

COL.title: Stories of resilience- Colombia CNTI
COL.description: Colombia’s 115 Indigenous Peoples have a deep relationship with their land, acting as guardians for approximately 60 million hectares in total. However, with the ongoing pandemic this work has not only been placed on hold, but the nationwide lockdown has created conditions for a resurgence of much of the violence, marginalisation and abuse that have beset indigenous populations for so long. The Tenure Facility’s partners are well used to swimming against the tide, and so work is underway to adapt to new realities that this pandemic has inflicted on us globally.

GUY.description: A session on "Dealing with security of land tenure during times of crisis" by Jean La Rose (English)

GUY.title: Stories of resilience- Guyana
GUY.description: Guyana’s dense forests have for generations been safeguarded by indigenous populations who make up around a tenth of the population. As the world wakes up to the need to protect these forests through climate funding, there have been renewed efforts to title indigenous land. This valuable work has been now challenged by the arrival of COVID-19 as it has hit indigenous communities hard. Luckily, the Tenure Facility´s partners, with their deep relations to the communities they work alongside have been able to respond, ensuring feedback from the communities even though they have been isolated. Thus the work of securing land tenure in the country can continue.

IND.title: Day 2 - India - Role of Technology in Sustaining Tenure
Stories of resilience- India
IND.description: The pandemic has had an enormous impact on the livelihoods of the local people in India, but it has also impacted the progress of the Land Rights project and the work of Tenure Facility’s partners. The two years they have spent building up relationships with the local people has been threatened by the pandemic. In order to not let this valuable network sit idle during the period of lockdown, they shifted their focus. The facilitators and volunteers have organized awareness drives in 1200 different villages where their network has been actively helping the district administration in this collective effort to stave off the danger of the Coronavirus.

LBR.title: Day 3 - Liberia (part 2) - Government and the Liberian People working towards and inclusive Liberia
Day 3 - Liberia (part 1) - Government and the Liberian People working towards an Inclusive Liberia
Day 2 - Liberia - Sustaining Tenure in Liberian Communities
Pilot project Liberia 2015
LBR.description: The goal for the pilot project in Liberia was to recognize, formalize, and strengthen customary collective community land and natural resource tenure rights. The project started in 2015 and ended in 2017. It was carried through by our partner Foundation for Community Initiatives (FCI).

LBR.title: Stories of resilience- Liberia
LBR.description: After decades of conflict over land which helped fuel a bitter civil war, in 2018 a new land law was passed in Liberia which meant that rural communities had the chance to gain greater control over their ancestral lands. The Tenure Facility backed project has placed the role of women at the heart of strengthening the capacity of these communities to title and manage their lands. But the arrival of COVID-19 has created severe challenges. Deadly diseases are nothing new in Liberia, but lockdown rules have left rural families short of vital food and medicine, and economic pressures have seen an ominous rise in sexual and gender-based violence. Nonetheless, our partners have been relying on the expertise they gained during the Ebola crisis to confront COVID-19 and its challenges to bring forward a brighter future.

MLI.title: Day 3 - Mali - Prévention et gestion des conflits fonciers par les communautés locales au Mali
Stories of resilience- Mali
MLI.description: It is difficult for information to reach remote rural areas in Mali, meaning that communities are often cut off from the outside world. A lack of awareness over land rights has created  tensions over land, in turn fueling armed conflict in the country. The emergence of COVID-19 has increased this problem with drastic measures taken by the Malian authorities and travel restricted, our partners have been confronting new realities and with this, they have resourced for new solutions. This has included COVID training for all staff, as well as for community focal points. Keeping communities informed as the pandemic continues will be crucial in their everyday work.

NPL.title: Day 1 - Nepal - Securing collective resources and land tenure right through Federalism in Nepal
Stories of resilience- Nepal
NPL.description:
After a decade of political upheaval, Nepal entered a phase of peace process and
stability which brought with it a new constitution that saw land reforms and tenure rights properly established in law. However, efforts to digitise land registration remain patchy. The legal rights of community forestry groups can be withdrawn at any time by forestry officials. This situation has been worsened by the arrival of the pandemic; however, the Tenure facility’s partners have been working to coordinate with the local communities and carry on with the project in the best way they can.

PAN.title: Day 2 - Panama - Gobernanza y defensa de los territorios
Stories of resilience- Panama
PAN.description: Panama has some of the world’s most progressive laws protecting indigenous rights. Yet in recent years pressure has been growing on the county’s indigenous Peoples - from the private sector, the landless poor, and the Government’s claims to protected areas. Nevertheless, Indigenous Peoples are uniting once more and building their capacity, making them a serious force to be reckoned with. An example of this, has been now with the pandemic, traditional practices have become central to their response. Many Indigenous Peoples have turned to traditional medicines to mitigate the impacts of the virus. While no one is suggesting that these medicines offer a cure to COVID-19, there use is a reminder of the extraordinary wisdom residing in indigenous cultures

PER.title: Day 2 - Peru - Comunidades resilientes en tiempos de cambio
Stories of resilience- Peru
PER.description: In Peru, the work to right historic wrongs against Indigenous Peoples, has been strengthened in the last years. Last year, the Peruvian President himself attended an emotional ceremony in the vast northern Loreto region to see 66 indigenous communities receive the title to their lands. But with the country been badly hit by the coronavirus, Indigenous populations are seeing resurgent threats to their lands, livelihoods and lives. During Coronavirus, the local authorities are doing what they can to provide assistance, but still, many communities are turning to traditional medicines. The pandemic has allowed Tenure Facility’s partners to reflect on the relevance of the issues at stake. The silver lining during this pandemic has been the government pursue of an ambitious plan to recognize the lands of all identified indigenous and peasant communities by 2021.
